questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

In 2014, the Hong Kong Housing Authority said the waiting time for public sector housing had increased and it would only complete 8900 flats of the 15000 planned for the year. The reasons were the shortage of workers because they were needed in other public sector projects, the difficulty of finding land, and government regulations. Which economic concepts are illustrated in this information?

options.A: a market economy and a lack of resources
options.B: economic planning and the price mechanism
options.C: opportunity cost of labour and excess demand
options.D: production possibility and budget deficit

questions.questionText: What is most likely to be a distinguishing feature of the healthcare system of a mixed economy?

options.A: a mixture of foreign and domestically owned hospitals
options.B: a mixture of foreign and domestic medical staff
options.C: a mixture of government-owned and privately owned hospitals
options.D: a mixture of specialist and general hospitals

questions.questionText: An economy can produce only two goods at any one time. These are good X and one other good from A, B, C or D. The table shows the outputs of goods A, B, C and D with each output of good X when the economy’s resources are fully employed. Which good must be produced with good X to show a production possibility curve with increasing costs? units X 0 100 200 300 400
What could not cause a shift in an individual’s demand curve for good Z?

options.A: a change in advertising expenditure on Z
options.B: a change in the individual’s income
options.C: a change in the individual’s tastes
options.D: a change in the price of Z

questions.questionText: What is most likely to increase the quantity of houses supplied?

options.A: a policy to help house buyers on modest incomes
options.B: a restriction on the level of rent that can be charged
options.C: a rise in the tax on materials used for building houses
options.D: the removal of a subsidy to house builders

questions.questionText: In which situation is the demand for a product said to be price elastic?

options.A: A fall in price increases expenditure on the product.
options.B: A fall in price increases quantity demanded.
options.C: A rise in price increases expenditure on the product.
options.D: A rise in price reduces quantity demanded.

questions.questionText: Goods X and Y are complements with a cross-elasticity of demand of –0.8. When the price of good X was $10, the quantity of good Y demanded was 2000 units per week. After a change in the price of good X, the demand for good Y increases to 2800 units per week. What is the new price of good X?

The diagram shows an industry’s total revenue when different quantities are demanded. point 2 point 1 point 3 total revenue O quantity demanded Which values should be inserted at points 1, 2 and 3 to identify the price elasticity of demand (PED) at that position? point 1 point 2 point 3

options.A: PED>1 PED=0 PED<1
options.B: PED>1 PED=1 PED<1
options.C: PED<1 PED=0 PED>1
options.D: PED<1 PED=1 PED>1

questions.questionText: What would increase the price elasticity of supply of a firm’s products?

options.A: a decrease in the period of time that stocks can be kept
options.B: a decrease in the time that it takes to produce the products
options.C: an increase in the cost of capital goods employed by the firm
options.D: an increase in the level of employment in the area

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the market for a luxury brand of smartphones. The initial equilibrium is at point X. What will be the new equilibrium following a rise in the price of batteries used by the manufacturer of smartphones and a rise in consumer incomes? supply A D price X B C demand O quantity
When will it not be possible to use price as a rationing mechanism?

options.A: when a good has a number of close substitutes
options.B: when a good is an inferior good
options.C: when the demand for a good is infinitely inelastic
options.D: when the quantity of a good is in fixed supply

questions.questionText: A government imposes an indirect tax on a product with normal demand and supply curves. The tax raises $100million. What effect will the tax have on the value of the combined consumer surplus and producer surplus?

options.A: It will be unaffected.
options.B: It will fall by less than $100million.
options.C: It will fall by exactly $100million.
options.D: It will fall by more than $100million.

questions.questionText: In the diagram, D is the demand curve of an agricultural commodity and S is the initial supply curve. The government promises to maintain farmers’ incomes at least at this initial level. The harvests in four subsequent years are shown by supply curves S –S .
The diagram shows the supply and demand curves of a commodity.

options.A: government subsidy causes the supply curve to shift from S to S .

questions.questionText: Total public spending in the UK, excluding interest payments, is planned to be £679 billion for the fiscal year 2015–2016. The table shows this by category. £billion pensions 150 healthcare 133 education 90 defence 46 social security welfare payments 110 other spending on goods and services 150 What was the total amount spent on transfer payments?

options.A: £110 billion B £150 billion C £260 billion D £393 billion

questions.questionText: Which government policy might limit the rationing function of the price mechanism?

options.A: the abolition of tariffs on imported consumer goods
options.B: the levy of indirect taxes at varying rates on different goods
options.C: the payment of subsidies to exporters
options.D: the setting of minimum prices for milk

questions.questionText: Which argument has often been used to justify the privatisation of state enterprises?

options.A: Private firms always aim at maximum profits.
options.B: Private firms can produce the same outputs at lower unit costs.
options.C: State enterprises are always monopolies which exploit consumers.
options.D: State enterprises cannot operate without government subsidies.

questions.questionText: A government plans to increase spending on education and training every year. Which diagram shows the likely effect of this increase on the economy’s long-run output and price level?

options.A: B LRAS LRAS LRAS

questions.questionText: In 2012, the rate of inflation in Botswana was 7.5%. Person X kept all of their savings in the form of cash while Person Y put their savings into a bank account on which they earned 5.0% interest. What was the effect on the real value of their savings by the end of the year? Person X Person Y

options.A: decrease decrease
options.B: decrease increase
options.C: no change decrease
options.D: no change increase

questions.questionText: The graph shows the annual percentage change in the prices of services and in the prices of goods between 2007 and 2012. services % annual 4 price change 2 2007 2008 2009 2010 2011 2012 –2 goods –4 What can be deduced from the graph?

options.A: On average the price of services was higher than the price of goods throughout the period.
options.B: The average price of goods was higher in 2012 than in 2010.
options.C: The average price of services was higher in 2012 than in 2010.
options.D: There was a fall in the general price level between 2008 and 2010.

questions.questionText: The table shows items from the balance of payments for countries A, B, C and D. Official financing including changes in reserves is excluded from the financial account. Which country has the greatest disequilibrium on its balance of payments? Current Account Capital Account Financial Account $million $million $million

An increase or decrease in exchange rates can take place in both a floating and a fixed exchange rate system but different terminology is used for each system. What is the correct terminology? decrease in floating increase in fixed

options.A: depreciation appreciation
options.B: depreciation revaluation
options.C: devaluation appreciation
options.D: devaluation revaluation

questions.questionText: In the diagram, curves D D and SS relate to the demand for and supply of £ sterling in the

The table shows the indices of import prices and export prices of four countries between July 2013 and July 2014. index of import prices index of export prices July 2013 July 2014 July 2013 July 2014 Brazil 137 139 164 162 China 98 101 99 99 Italy 113 111 113 114 Spain 110 106 111 109 In which countries did the terms of trade improve between July 2013 and July 2014?

options.A: Brazil and China
options.B: China only
options.C: Italy and Spain
options.D: Italy only

questions.questionText: Country X can produce apples and plums at lower cost than country Y. Country X can also produce strawberries but it costs more to do so than in country Y. In fact, country X produces only apples and trades them for plums and strawberries from country Y. What economic analysis could explain this pattern of trade? plums strawberries

options.A: absolute advantage country X absolute advantage country X
options.B: absolute advantage country Y comparative advantage country Y
options.C: comparative advantage country Y absolute advantage country Y
options.D: comparative advantage country Y comparative advantage country X

questions.questionText: A government wants to use trade protection both to improve its trade performance and to raise government revenue. Which policy will help it to achieve this?

options.A: raising quotas on imported goods
options.B: raising subsidies on exported goods
options.C: raising tariffs on exported goods
options.D: raising tariffs on imported goods

questions.questionText: A newly-built public sector engineering training college received poor inspection reports. The government ceased to pay the college the money that it had usually received as its annual grant. Which types of government policy does this statement imply?

options.A: fiscal and monetary policies only
options.B: fiscal and supply-side policies only
options.C: fiscal, monetary and supply-side policies
options.D: monetary and supply-side policies only

questions.questionText: Which measure to correct a balance of payments current account deficit would be classified as an expenditure-dampening policy?

options.A: a reduction in interest rates
options.B: a revaluation of the currency
options.C: an increase in direct taxes
options.D: an introduction of foreign exchange controls

questions.questionText: A government is faced with rising inflation. It wishes to reduce inflationary pressure while avoiding a rise in unemployment. Which action is most likely to meet its needs?

options.A: an increase in employment taxes
options.B: an increase in laws to promote competition
options.C: an increase in the budget surplus
